scenes.tts: A receptor has let go, yet a G protein remains active. What decides when that already-loaded switch stops? Follow that molecule beneath the membrane and watch its active interval. The answer lies inside the nucleotide the protein carries.
scenes.caption: A receptor has let go, yet a G protein remains active. What decides when that already-loaded switch stops? Follow that molecule beneath the membrane and watch its active interval. The answer lies inside the nucleotide the protein carries.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP: GDP/off = slate; GTP/on = gold; GEF action = teal; GAP action = clay-red. Fill the frame with a membrane bar and one large slate G-protein block beneath it. A receptor releases its ligand and dims, while the block's small schematic activity trace remains above baseline. Label the trace 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A receptor has let go, yet a G protein remains active. What decides when that already-loaded switch stops? Follow that molecule beneath the membrane and watch its active interval. The answer lies inside the nucleotide the protein carries.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the same moving membrane world: The Timer Inside the Switch. The slate block drifts slowly beneath the membrane; do not reset the layout.

scenes.tts: Start with the switch off. It holds GDP, shown as a slate token with its phosphate tabs. The protein grips that token tightly, so exchange is slow without help. That resting complex waits beside the receptor in the membrane.
scenes.caption: Start with the switch off. It holds GDP, shown as a slate token with its phosphate tabs. The protein grips that token tightly, so exchange is slow without help. That resting complex waits beside the receptor in the membrane.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto the carried slate block. A labelled GDP token with two square phosphate tabs settles into a deep pocket. A faint closed hand shape around the token tightens, while a slow teal loading gauge stays near zero. Mark every token and trace 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Start with the switch off. It holds GDP, shown as a slate token with its phosphate tabs. The protein grips that token tightly, so exchange is slow without help. That resting complex waits beside the receptor in the membrane.

scenes.tts: An occupied receptor acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, or GEF. It opens the grip and promotes GDP release. GTP, far more plentiful than GDP, then takes the empty place. The receptor promotes exchange; it does not hand over GTP.
scenes.caption: An occupied receptor acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, or GEF. It opens the grip and promotes GDP release. GTP, far more plentiful than GDP, then takes the empty place. The receptor promotes exchange; it does not hand over GTP.
scenes.visual: Restore the ligand to the receptor. A teal GEF pulse travels down, pries the block's grip open, and lifts GDP out. A gold GTP token with three phosphate tabs floats from a moving cytosolic pool into the empty pocket. The receptor never carries GTP.
scenes.narration: An occupied receptor acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, or GEF. It opens the grip and promotes GDP release. GTP, far more plentiful than GDP, then takes the empty place. The receptor promotes exchange; it does not hand over GTP.

scenes.tts: GTP changes the protein's shape. The block turns gold, its activity trace rises, and a target beside it switches on. This GTP-bound interval is the state we will time. Alpha and beta-gamma can each regulate targets after the rearrangement.
scenes.caption: GTP changes the protein's shape. The block turns gold, its activity trace rises, and a target beside it switches on. This GTP-bound interval is the state we will time. Alpha and beta-gamma can each regulate targets after the rearrangement.
scenes.visual: The block smoothly widens and changes from slate to gold. A nearby target dial rotates from OFF to ON. Above them, a gold schematic trace rises and extends rightward as a live time bar, with a moving dot at its leading edge.
scenes.narration: GTP changes the protein's shape. The block turns gold, its activity trace rises, and a target beside it switches on. This GTP-bound interval is the state we will time. Alpha and beta-gamma can each regulate targets after the rearrangement.

scenes.tts: The G protein is also an enzyme, a GTPase. After a variable wait, it cuts off GTP's last phosphate. GDP remains, the shape relaxes, and the target turns off. Cutting always returns this switch to its GDP-bound state.
scenes.caption: The G protein is also an enzyme, a GTPase. After a variable wait, it cuts off GTP's last phosphate. GDP remains, the shape relaxes, and the target turns off. Cutting always returns this switch to its GDP-bound state.
scenes.visual: Keep the gold interval growing, with a subtle irregular shimmer to show a variable wait. The third tab detaches and drifts away. The token relabels GDP, the block transforms back to slate, the target dial returns to OFF, and the schematic trace falls.
scenes.narration: The G protein is also an enzyme, a GTPase. After a variable wait, it cuts off GTP's last phosphate. GDP remains, the shape relaxes, and the target turns off. Cutting always returns this switch to its GDP-bound state.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule for that loaded molecule. Faster GTP cutting shortens an already-loaded GTPase's time on. Loading starts the interval; hydrolysis ends it. The rule does not say how often loading begins.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule for that loaded molecule. Faster GTP cutting shortens an already-loaded GTPase's time on. Loading starts the interval; hydrolysis ends it. The rule does not say how often loading begins.
scenes.visual: Build a large horizontal interval from two carried markers: teal 'GTP loaded' at the left and slate 'GTP cut' at the right. The gold span between them contracts as a cutting-speed slider moves right. Label the interval and slider 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule for that loaded molecule. Faster GTP cutting shortens an already-loaded GTPase's time on. Loading starts the interval; hydrolysis ends it. The rule does not say how often loading begins.

scenes.tts: Now compare matched gold switches. A GAP approaches only the lower switch and accelerates its cutting reaction. Both begin with the same GTP and target. Which gold interval should end sooner? Hold your answer.
scenes.caption: Now compare matched gold switches. A GAP approaches only the lower switch and accelerates its cutting reaction. Both begin with the same GTP and target. Which gold interval should end sooner? Hold your answer.
scenes.visual: Split the carried world into two aligned rows with identical gold blocks and equally growing schematic traces. A clay-red GAP block moves beside only the lower GTPase. Put the question above both rows; traces keep extending during narration.
scenes.narration: Now compare matched gold switches. A GAP approaches only the lower switch and accelerates its cutting reaction. Both begin with the same GTP and target. Which gold interval should end sooner? Hold your answer.

scenes.visual: Keep the question visible. Both gold blocks pulse gently and both schematic traces creep right at the same speed. The GAP hovers beside the lower switch without revealing the outcome.

scenes.tts: The lower interval ends first. The GAP does not remove GTP or supply fuel. It helps the GTPase reach the cutting transition faster, then leaves GDP behind. The products are unchanged; only the speed differs.
scenes.caption: The lower interval ends first. The GAP does not remove GTP or supply fuel. It helps the GTPase reach the cutting transition faster, then leaves GDP behind. The products are unchanged; only the speed differs.
scenes.visual: The lower third phosphate tab detaches first; its block turns slate and its trace falls. The upper trace continues gold. Show a clay-red chevron accelerating the lower cut, then move the GAP away while GDP stays in the pocket.
scenes.narration: The lower interval ends first. The GAP does not remove GTP or supply fuel. It helps the GTPase reach the cutting transition faster, then leaves GDP behind. The products are unchanged; only the speed differs.

scenes.tts: For first-order cutting, the average active time is the reciprocal of the cutting rate constant. A larger rate constant means a shorter mean interval. The exact wait still varies among molecules. Fewer molecules remain active at each later time.
scenes.caption: For first-order cutting, the average active time is the reciprocal of the cutting rate constant. A larger rate constant means a shorter mean interval. The exact wait still varies among molecules. Fewer molecules remain active at each later time.
scenes.visual: Replace the two rows with a computed family of exponential survival curves, using arbitrary rate constants and no spoken values. Label axes 'time' and 'fraction still GTP-bound'; label the plot 'computed example'. Animate a rate slider upward as the curve steepens.
scenes.narration: For first-order cutting, the average active time is the reciprocal of the cutting rate constant. A larger rate constant means a shorter mean interval. The exact wait still varies among molecules. Fewer molecules remain active at each later time.

scenes.tts: A whole-cell response has other clocks. Receptors can reload many switches, targets can turn off, and messengers can be cleared. Those clocks also shape the pathway-level trace. Our rule isolates a single already-loaded GTPase's lifetime.
scenes.caption: A whole-cell response has other clocks. Receptors can reload many switches, targets can turn off, and messengers can be cleared. Those clocks also shape the pathway-level trace. Our rule isolates a single already-loaded GTPase's lifetime.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the membrane. Show several gold switches being loaded, a target dial, and messenger dots fading. Bracket only one gold block and its interval in bright white; dim the other processes without crossing them out.
scenes.narration: A whole-cell response has other clocks. Receptors can reload many switches, targets can turn off, and messengers can be cleared. Those clocks also shape the pathway-level trace. Our rule isolates a single already-loaded GTPase's lifetime.

scenes.tts: That distinction makes experiments readable. Change loading, and you change how often switches start. Change GTP cutting, and you change how long each loaded switch remains active. Keeping those controls separate prevents a common reasoning error.
scenes.caption: That distinction makes experiments readable. Change loading, and you change how often switches start. Change GTP cutting, and you change how long each loaded switch remains active. Keeping those controls separate prevents a common reasoning error.
scenes.visual: Two controls appear beside the same carried switch. A teal loading control changes the spacing between new gold intervals. A clay-red cutting control changes each interval's width. Both animations remain labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: That distinction makes experiments readable. Change loading, and you change how often switches start. Change GTP cutting, and you change how long each loaded switch remains active. Keeping those controls separate prevents a common reasoning error.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only, large and centered: 'Faster GTP cutting shortens an already-loaded GTPase's time on.' No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
